evidence.title: Ferrari F1 continuerà a sviluppare la SF-26: cosa significa davvero l’annuncio di Vasseur
evidence.body: [e002:f01] Il team principal della Scuderia ha confermato che la SF-26 continuerà a ricevere aggiornamenti fino alla fine della stagione, una scelta che ha sorpreso gran parte degli addetti ai lavori. [e002:f02] Contents Vasseur cambia la strategia Ferrari sulla SF-26 Perché Ferrari continua a portare aggiornamenti Gli aggiornamenti Ferrari non si fermano a Baku Cosa significa questa scelta in ottica Mondiale Ferrari manda un messaggio a McLaren e Red Bull Nel corso della puntata Race Tech #167, l’ingegnere Riccardo Romanelli ha spiegato perché questo annuncio rappresenta molto più di una semplice conferma sul piano dello sviluppo tecnico della Ferrari. [e002:f03] Vasseur cambia la strategia Ferrari sulla SF-26 Tradizionalmente, nella seconda parte della stagione i team iniziano a spostare uomini e risorse sul progetto dell’anno successivo. [e002:f04] Nel 2026, però, Ferrari ha deciso di seguire una strada diversa. [e002:f05] Secondo quanto spiegato da Vasseur, la SF-26 non è ancora arrivata al limite del proprio potenziale e continuerà a essere sviluppata gara dopo gara fino all’ultimo appuntamento del Mondiale. [e002:f06] Una scelta che, secondo Romanelli, indica chiaramente la volontà di Ferrari di non interrompere la crescita della monoposto. [e002:f07] Da una parte significa che gli ingegneri di Maranello hanno individuato ancora margini di miglioramento sulla SF-26. [e002:f08] Dall’altra dimostra che il team ritiene gli aggiornamenti sufficientemente efficaci da giustificare l’investimento fino al termine della stagione. È un messaggio importante anche nei confronti della concorrenza: Ferrari non considera chiuso lo sviluppo della vettura. [e002:f09] Durante Race Tech #167 viene spiegato che Ferrari continuerà a introdurre evoluzioni anche nelle gare successive, lavorando su più aree della monoposto per migliorare prestazioni ed efficienza. [e002:f10] L’obiettivo è arrivare alle ultime gare con una SF-26 ancora competitiva nella lotta al vertice. [e002:f11] Cosa significa questa scelta in ottica Mondiale Continuare lo sviluppo fino alla fine comporta inevitabilmente una gestione molto attenta delle risorse. [e002:f12] Secondo Romanelli, Ferrari ha deciso di non anticipare completamente il lavoro sul progetto successivo, preferendo sfruttare ogni opportunità per migliorare la SF-26 durante il campionato in corso. È una strategia che punta a massimizzare il rendimento della monoposto senza rinunciare alla possibilità di raccogliere risultati importanti nelle ultime gare. [e002:f13] Ferrari manda un messaggio a McLaren e Red Bull L’annuncio di Vasseur arriva nello stesso weekend in cui McLaren presenta uno dei pacchetti aerodinamici più estesi della stagione a Baku. mclaren F1 contro Ferrari F1 2026 disegno di Salvatore Asero Ferrari risponde con una scelta diversa ma altrettanto significativa: gli sviluppi continueranno fino all’ultima gara del Mondiale. evidence.title: FIA WEC: Qualifying in Fuji cancelled due to poor weather
evidence.body: [e003:f01] The #36 of Alpine Endurance Team will start from pole position for the 6 Hours of Fuji , with the grid set by the fastest time across all practice sessions, following the cancellation of Qualifying. [e003:f02] Qualifying for the 6 Hours of Fuji has been called off because of due to poor weather conditions, with the starting grid for the race being determined by the combined results from all three practice sessions that took place on Friday and earlier Saturday morning. [e003:f03] It's a first ever pole position for the A424 Alpine Hypercar, with Victor Martins' lap of 1.40:694 from FP2 securing it. [e003:f04] The decision followed an early red flag in LMGT3 qualifying after Francois Heriau crashed the #21 AF Corse Ferrari 296 GT3 Evo at Turn 2. [e003:f05] Heriau appeared to lose control after his car aquaplaned while exiting Turn 1, sending the Ferrari into the barrier on the right-hand side of the circuit. [e003:f06] The French driver was able to climb out of the car unharmed. [e003:f07] Race control subsequently confirmed that the session would not restart and that qualifying had been cancelled because of the worsening conditions. [e003:f08] As a result, the grid will be formed using the combined practice times.

previous_updates.title: F1、地域紛争を受け2026年バーレーンGPを中止
previous_updates.summary: F1は地域紛争の再燃を受け、2026年バーレーンGPの開催を断念した。 バーレーン戦の中止は2011年以来で、カタール、アブダビ戦の開催にも不透明感が残る。

previous_updates.title: Haas、2027年のF1起用へFornaroliと基本合意との報道
previous_updates.summary: HaasはMcLaren育成のLeonardo Fornaroliを2027年に起用する方向で基本合意し、McLarenとの契約調整を進めていると報じられた。 現段階はレター・オブ・インテントで契約成立ではなく、ハースF1はオリバー・ベアマンの残留を軸にエステバン・オコンの後任を検討している。

evidence.title: 「ＹＥＢＩＳＵ ビアグルメグランプリ」決定、「笑酒屋 極限流 祖師谷支部」の自家製ピンクタルタルたっぷり絶品チキン南蛮が頂点に
evidence.body: [e007:f01] 来場者投票の結果、「笑酒屋（えぐしや） 極限流 祖師谷支部」の自家製ピンクタルタルたっぷり絶品チキン南蛮がグランプリに選ばれた。 [e007:f02] 同グランプリは、飲食店とヱビスが共創する食のイベント。 [e007:f03] 決勝ステージには４店舗が出店し、ヱビスビールに合わせて考案したメニューが来場者に提供された。 [e007:f04] 「笑酒屋 極限流 祖師谷支部」（東京・砧）の志治英明店主は「本当に全ての皆さんに感謝をしたいと思っています」と感慨深げ。 [e007:f05] 悪天候が続いたが、「たくさんのお客様に来ていただいて、たくさんの笑顔を見させていただくことができました」としみじみと語った。 [e007:f06] 初日の来場者が再び会場を訪れたエピソードを紹介。 [e007:f07] 「あまりにもおいしかったので家族を連れてきた」と声をかけられたといい、「１回食べて、改めて違う日に来ていただけるお客様が何人かいらっしゃって。 [e007:f08] こんなうれしいことはない」と感激していた。 [e007:f09] 記事に関するキーワード 恵比寿ガーデンプレイス 東京都渋谷区 東京都 関東甲信越 提供元の記事 （外部サイトに移動します）。

evidence.title: クリスチャン・ホーナー フェラーリF1代表就任に意欲「唯一の例外。夢のチーム」
evidence.body: [e009:f01] クリスチャン・ホーナーが、F1への本格復帰にあたって原則として求めている「オーナーシップへの参加」という条件について、フェラーリだけは例外になると明かした。 [e009:f02] ホーナーはフェラーリを「F1最大のブランド」「夢」と表現し、チームを率いる可能性に明確に扉を開いた。 [e009:f03] によれば、この発言はフェラーリでフレデリック・バスールの将来を巡る憶測が再び強まっているタイミングで飛び出した。

evidence.title: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援
evidence.body: [e001:f01] 6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 [e001:f02] 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 [e001:f03] ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。 [e001:f04] 電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。 [e001:f05] アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。 [e001:f06] ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 [e001:f07] 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 [e001:f08] 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。 [e001:f09] ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 [e001:f10] 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。 [e001:f11] 2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。

evidence.title: NASA and SpaceX Prepare Crew-13 for Launch to the International Space Station
evidence.body: [e001:f01] The mission will launch on a Falcon 9 rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, continuing the operational sequence of NASA’s Commercial Crew Program. [e001:f02] From left are, Commander Jessica Watkins and Pilot Luke Delaney, both from NASA, and Mission Specialists Joshua Kutryk of CSA (Canadian Space Agency) and Sergey Teteryatnikov of Roscosmos. [e001:f03] NASA But Crew-13 carries an additional historical significance. [e001:f04] Its official mission patch includes a tribute to Apollo 13, the 1970 lunar mission that became one of the most dramatic examples of engineering, teamwork and survival in the history of human spaceflight. [e001:f05] More than five decades after Apollo 13, NASA is once again flying a crewed mission designated with the number 13 — this time without changing the designation or avoiding the number. [e001:f06] Rather than treating 13 as a warning sign, the Crew-13 emblem uses the legacy of Apollo 13 as a reminder of how engineering and human ingenuity can overcome extraordinary circumstances. [e001:f07] The legacy of Apollo 13 The association between NASA and the number 13 became particularly strong in April 1970. [e001:f08] Two days later, on April 13, an oxygen tank in the spacecraft’s Service Module exploded, severely damaging the vehicle and forcing NASA to abandon the planned lunar landing. [e001:f09] Although Apollo 13 failed to achieve its planned lunar landing, NASA ultimately regarded the mission as a remarkable demonstration of engineering capability and crisis management. [e001:f10] When NASA briefly avoided the number 13 The space agency’s relationship with the number 13 became more complicated during the Space Shuttle era. [e001:f11] After the first shuttle missions were designated sequentially as STS-1, STS-2 and so on, NASA introduced a different naming system in the early 1980s. [e001:f12] The new system incorporated elements such as the fiscal year, launch site and mission sequence. [e001:f13] One of the most memorable responses came from the crew of STS-41-C, which launched in April 1984. [e001:f14] SpaceX’s crewed Dragon missions began with the Demo-2 test flight in 2020, followed by the operational Crew-1 mission and subsequent flights. [e001:f15] Crew-13 therefore represents more than another entry in the launch manifest. [e001:f16] For engineers, flight controllers and astronauts, the critical factors remain the same: propulsion performance, trajectory calculations, spacecraft systems, redundancy, weather conditions, communications and continuous monitoring of the vehicle.

evidence.title: Vietjet signs with Starlink to bring free high-speed Wi-Fi to its entire network
evidence.body: [e002:f01] The agreement was signed in New York on 23 September 2026 between SpaceX, which engineers and operates the Starlink network, and Vietjet together with its group companies Galaxy Holdings and Galaxy Telecom. [e002:f02] Vietnam's General Secretary and President To Lam attended the exchange during his working visit to the United States, joined by senior officials and business leaders from both countries, giving the deal a diplomatic profile that few airline connectivity contracts ever achieve. ## 120 aircraft in the first wave Starlink will first be fitted to 120 Vietjet aircraft, comprising 100 narrowbody Airbus A321 and Boeing 737 jets alongside 20 Airbus A330 widebodies that operate the airline's longer international sectors. [e002:f03] Vietjet plans to equip every new aircraft it takes delivery of with the system, so connectivity will grow in step with the fleet across both its Vietnamese domestic network and its fast-expanding international map. [e002:f04] Starlink's satellites sit in low Earth orbit, much closer to the ground than the geostationary satellites behind most traditional inflight Wi-Fi systems, which gives the service the low latency needed for video calls and streaming in the cabin. [e002:f05] Vietjet will offer the service free of charge on every Vietjet-branded flight, with the airline setting out an ambition to make fast inflight Wi-Fi an everyday part of air travel that every traveller can use. [e002:f06] Vietjet Chairwoman Dr Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao said: "With Starlink, time in the air no longer has to mean time offline. [e002:f07] Vietjet passengers will be able to stay connected throughout their journey, whether working, staying entertained, or keeping in touch with family and friends. [e002:f08] This reflects Vietjet's longstanding commitment to innovation and our ambition to bring leading technologies closer to more people." ! [e002:f09] [Image 1](https:// Vietjet and SpaceX exchanged the agreement to bring high-speed internet to Vietjet flights, in the presence of Vietnam's General Secretary and President To Lam, senior officials and business leaders from Vietnam and the United States. [e002:f10] "We're thrilled to deliver a connectivity experience to Vietjet and its customers, making every journey better, smoother and infinitely more enjoyable." Vietjet describes the agreement as the beginning of a long-term technology relationship with SpaceX, which sits alongside its continued investment in data, artificial intelligence and skilled talent as it builds what it calls a digital aviation ecosystem for the millions of passengers it carries each year. ## A network and fleet on the move The Starlink deal arrives during one of the busiest growth periods in Vietjet's history. [e002:f11] Australian travellers have more to look forward to as well, with Ho Chi Minh City to Western Sydney International launching on 9 January 2027. [e002:f12] Vietjet has ordered 100 Airbus A321neo aircraft, signed a US$3.8 billion Trent 7000 engine agreement with Rolls-Royce for its widebody fleet and selected Pratt & Whitney to power 44 further A320neo family jets, while its partnership with CFM International explores maintenance capability for the latest-generation LEAP engines in Vietnam. [e002:f13] Passengers can choose from Eco, Deluxe, SkyBoss and Business fares, with the SkyJoy loyalty programme rewarding frequent flyers across the network. ## Recognised by AirlineRatings Vietjet's growth has come without any compromise on safety. [e002:f14] The airline has held a seven-star safety rating with AirlineRatings since 2018, and in January it was named among the World's Safest Airlines for 2026, ranking alongside easyJet, Southwest Airlines and Ryanair. [e002:f15] Announcing the result, then AirlineRatings CEO Sharon Petersen said: "Vietjet Air has delivered steady growth while maintaining fleet continuity and a high level of operational reliability." In March Vietjet was named World's Best Ultra Low-Cost Carrier for 2026, a title it has held every year since 2018, and earned a place in the top ten World's Best Low-Cost Airlines for 2026. [e002:f16] With free satellite Wi-Fi now joining a safety record and product offering that have earned recognition from both our editorial panel and our readers, Vietjet is giving travellers across Asia and beyond one more reason to choose the airline for their next journey.

evidence.title: Starlink Mobile Launches in Uganda via Airtel Partnership
evidence.body: [e003:f01] The service went live on September 24, 2026, through a partnership with Airtel Uganda, targeting rural and remote communities where conventional cell coverage doesn't reach. [e003:f02] For the millions of Ugandans without reliable mobile internet, it's a meaningful shift — satellite connectivity delivered through an existing carrier relationship, no dish required. [e003:f03] Source: @Starlink — September 24, 2026 ▶ Watch Video on X The Deal Behind the Launch This isn't a standalone rollout — it's the first visible output of a broader agreement. [e003:f04] According to reporting from Space in Africa and TechAfrica News, Airtel Africa and SpaceX formalized a partnership in December 2025 to bring Starlink Direct-to-Cell across all 14 of Airtel Africa's operating markets. [e003:f05] Uganda is the first of those 14 markets to go live under this arrangement, following the Democratic Republic of Congo, which Starlink cited as the continent's first launch. [e003:f06] Airtel Uganda acts as the distribution and billing layer, meaning subscribers access the service through their existing Airtel relationship rather than setting up a separate Starlink account. [e003:f07] For those communities, Starlink Mobile offers something genuinely new: apps and messaging over satellite, using the phone already in hand. [e003:f08] The use cases Starlink highlighted in its announcement are deliberately modest — apps and messaging, not streaming — which reflects both the current capability ceiling of Direct-to-Cell and a realistic picture of what rural connectivity needs look like. [e003:f09] For SpaceX, carrier partnerships convert what would otherwise be a hardware-dependent consumer product into a wholesale connectivity layer — a fundamentally different business model than selling Starlink terminals to individual households. [e003:f10] What Comes Next With Uganda live and the DRC preceding it, the Airtel Africa rollout is now officially underway. [e003:f11] The remaining 12 markets in Airtel's footprint — which span Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, and others — represent the next wave of potential launches, though no specific timelines have been announced publicly. [e003:f12] For SpaceX, the Africa push is also a proof-of-concept for the carrier partnership model globally. [e003:f13] The Uganda launch is small in isolation — but as the second data point in a 14-market rollout, it's worth watching closely. evidence.title: SpaceX Preparing for Most Important Launch in Company History on Monday
evidence.body: [e004:f01] By Victor Tangermann Published Sep 25, 2026 10:51 AM EDT Add Futurism (opens in a new tab) SpaceX It feels like SpaceX’s Starship development has been in a bit of a holding pattern as of late. [e004:f02] The company’s most recent launch in July, which was its thirteenth full-scale test in almost three and a half years, saw the spacecraft successfully deploy 20 operational satellites. [e004:f03] But only ten out of its Super Heavy booster’s 13 Raptor engines relit during its landing, causing it to make a hard impact and explode. [e004:f04] Now the space company is looking to finally stick the landing. [e004:f05] This coming Monday, the company is planning to launch its fourteenth test flight, “ pending regulatory approval .” The plan is to have Starship circle the Earth a full six times over ten hours at an altitude of 171 miles before lightly touching down. [e004:f06] It’s almost certainly the biggest test of the launch platform yet, and arguably the most important launch in the company’s history. [e004:f07] Proving its orbital flight capabilities is mission critical if SpaceX ever wants Starship to deliver satellites at a regular cadence. [e004:f08] It’s also a key aspect of NASA’s planned Artemis 3 mission, which is currently slated for 2027 , a key stepping stone in the space agency’s ambitions to return astronauts to the lunar surface. [e004:f09] But give the sheer number of challenges SpaceX still has to overcome, from reliably entering orbit to sticking the landing of both its spacecraft and its booster, SpaceX may need to buy itself some more time before it can get NASA astronauts aboard its spacecraft in the Earth’s orbit next year. [e004:f10] SpaceX successfully conducted a full wet dress rehearsal earlier this week ahead of its Monday launch attempt. [e004:f11] Without igniting any engines, the company’s team ran through the countdown procedures to ensure everything’s ready. [e004:f12] Learning from its previous test launch, SpaceX modified the hardware of its Super Heavy booster to ensure all of its engines light up and guide it safely for a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. [e004:f13] “The Super Heavy on this upcoming flight has hardware modifications to improve filtering to the engines and software changes to enhance relight reliability,” the company’s website reads . [e004:f14] The company will even reuse two heatshield tiles that it recovered from its previous test launch, the “first tile reuse for Starship.” It will also deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites to “greatly expand the network’s capacity and user speeds.” A lot is riding on the success of next week’s launch. [e004:f15] The company is preparing to wind down its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket in favor of its much larger Starship platform, which can theoretically deliver roughly ten times as many satellites per launch. [e004:f16] More on Starship: SpaceX Is Learning a Nasty Lesson About Going Public When Your Main Product Is Experimental。

evidence.title: Report reveals that one of investor's biggest fears about SpaceX stock never actually happened.
evidence.body: [e001:f01] The SpaceX IPO was so big that investors worried it could reshape overall market structure. [e001:f02] Morningstar says the impact so far has been limited. [e001:f03] SpaceX stock has had a volatile ride since its record-setting debut this summer. [e001:f04] Elon Musk's rocket and AI company was hot out of the gate, but didn't sustain its momentum for long. [e001:f05] Importantly for investors watching from the sidelines, the splashy IPO hasn't reshaped the market in the way many had feared it might leading up to the debut. [e001:f06] Morningstar on Wednesday flagged that SpaceX's colossal market cap didn't translate into the overweighting at the index level many investors had been concerned about. [e001:f07] This was a worry percolating in the market as index providers changed their rules to fast track the stock into major averages like the Nasdaq 100. [e001:f08] "Despite reaching a $2 trillion market cap on its first day of trading, limited public float meant SpaceX represented only about 0.1% of the Total Market Index at the end of August, despite earlier fears surrounding its expedited inclusion in indexes," stated director of analytics Alex Poukchanski. [e001:f09] The concern was that funds that track the indexes would be forced to buy SpaceX, leaving investors exposed to the company even if they weren't interested in the IPO. [e001:f10] Given that popular indexes like the Nasdaq 100 are cap-weighted, there were fears that index funds would end up dumping other stocks to make room for SpaceX with its enormous market capitalization. [e001:f11] The fear has been mostly unfounded, for now. [e001:f12] For investors, this is a good sign ahead of other mega-IPOs, and rule changes might not be the market-breaking force some feared. [e001:f13] But Poukchanski added that extreme concentration is still a risk in the era of giant tech IPOs. [e001:f14] Giants like Anthropic and OpenAI will likely overshadow smaller offerings, and exacerbate that risk, he said. [e001:f15] "With anticipated IPOs from Anthropic and OpenAI, alongside continued subdued small-cap IPO activity, top-level market concentration could continue to rise, requiring further adjustments to the mega-cap segment to keep the indexes aligned with the market," Poukchanski added.

evidence.title: NTN update: Senate preps China ban; certification and testing; Starlink operators and geopolitics
evidence.body: [e002:f01] The US has banned Huawei et al; 3GPP standardization is in process, plus testing too; Japan and Europe want their own systems; and Starlink is all over the place, in commercial operators and geo-politics. [e002:f02] In sum – what to know: Regulation – The US Senate’s Secure Space Act would extend FCC security restrictions to satellite licenses, market access and earth stations tied to Covered List entities. [e002:f03] Certification – GCF, MSSA and companies including Particle and Skylo are building the standards, testing, and certification to make different flavors of NTN interoperable. [e002:f04] Commercial scale – Starlink is pushing D2D into more markets, notably in Africa, as Japan and Europe develop alternative satellite-connectivity ecosystems. [e002:f05] The US Senate has passed legislation to put a new security gate around satellite connectivity , essentially to stretch the US ban on Chinese tech to space systems. [e002:f06] The list includes Chinese vendors Huawei and ZTE, plus operators including China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom – among other (Chinese and non-Chinese) companies and categories of comms equipment and services. [e002:f07] The Global Certification Forum (GCF) and Mobile Satellite Services Association (MSSA) have signed a cooperation deal (MoU) to develop certification requirements and testing frameworks for standards-based NTN services. [e002:f08] Their work covers the two main 3GPP approaches: NTN 5G NR, aimed at broadband data and voice applications, and NTN NB-IoT, for low-power IoT devices. [e002:f09] They want a scalable certification model to support interoperability and roaming with terrestrial networks, as well as between different NTN constellations. [e002:f10] GCF has had NTN NB-IoT conformance testing for GEO systems since 2024; it wants to extend certification to NGSO/LEO systems, and to add NTN 5G NR. [e002:f11] Airtel Africa launched Starlink Mobile in the Democratic Republic of Congo in August – as the first commercial Starlink Mobile deployment in Africa, says Airtel. [e002:f12] The firm signed with Starlink in December (2025), testing the service in Kenya in March. [e002:f13] Meanwhile, Starlink has told maritime customers they can expect gigabit-per-second throughput with their $2,000 (Performance Gen 3) ground terminals by the end of the year, once SpaceX’s new V3 satellites are in service. (This is for conventional broadband connectivity via a physical terminal; not Starlink Mobile.) The company’s network expansion is happening in tandem with its more fraught and complex role in geopolitical comms and security. [e002:f14] Elsewhere, Finnish president Alexander Stubb has asked SpaceX to expand Starlink coverage in areas where Ukraine wants to target Russian ballistic-missile launchers. (And in a speech at the UN General Assembly, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu displayed a Starlink Mini while discussing internet access in Iran.) Resilience and sovereignty Meanwhile, Japan is putting government money behind an alternative approach, with its comms ministry supporting development of compact universal satellite antennas . [e002:f15] In September it agreed with South Korea to examine future integration, including technical cooperation and use cases. [e002:f16] Which puts Europe on a different track from Starlink’s vertically integrated model: a publicly backed strategic connectivity play built around European institutions, governments and industry partners, with security and resilience as the rationale.

evidence.title: Finnish President Urges Musk to Expand Starlink So Ukraine Can Strike Russian Missile Launchers
evidence.body: [e004:f01] We bring you stories from the ground. [e004:f02] Your support keeps our team in the field. [e004:f03] DONATE NOW Stubb made the appeal in an interview with Reuters in New York, where world leaders had gathered for the United Nations General Assembly. [e004:f04] He argued that expanded Starlink coverage could help Ukraine locate and target mobile launchers operating from Russian territory before they fire missiles. [e004:f05] According to Reuters, Starlink currently does not operate over Russian territory. [e004:f06] Ukrainian officials believe enabling the service there would allow Ukrainian weapons to strike mobile ballistic missile launchers located within several hundred kilometers of the border. [e004:f07] Now They Need to Fly Into Russia Aug 19, 2026 11:04 Stubb said allowing Ukraine to use Starlink in areas where ballistic missile launchers operate, including temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory and Russia, could save lives. [e004:f08] He argued that the capability could, “to a certain extent,” serve as a form of air defense by helping Ukraine target launchers before missiles are fired. [e004:f09] The appeal comes as Ukraine prepares for another winter of Russian attacks on its energy and heating infrastructure. [e004:f10] Reuters reported that Russian ballistic missile strikes reached record levels during the summer, while Ukraine faces a shortage of interceptors. [e004:f11] Stubb identified three priorities for Ukraine ahead of winter: strengthening air defenses, protecting energy infrastructure, and securing financing. [e004:f12] He said an unconditional ceasefire would be the simplest starting point, followed by negotiations over security guarantees, territorial issues, reconstruction, and compensation. [e004:f13] The Finnish president’s appeal follows earlier Ukrainian efforts to secure expanded Starlink access for operations against Russian missile launchers. [e004:f14] In late July, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy asked US President Donald Trump during closed-door White House talks to help secure Musk’s approval for expanded Starlink use, The Atlantic reported at the time. [e004:f15] The proposal was intended to help Ukraine target mobile Russian ballistic missile launchers before winter. [e004:f16] Trump gave no firm commitment during the meeting and said he would consider the request and discuss it with Musk, according to officials cited in the earlier reporting.

evidence.title: Launches FALCON Verify to Bring Trust, Reliability, and Verification to AI-Generated Answers
evidence.body: [e001:f01] One Intelligence | today announced the availability of FALCON Verify, a new AI verification capability designed to address a fundamental challenge with generative AI: an AI answer can sound convincing even when part, or all of it is wrong. [e001:f02] FALCON Verify works inside ChatGPT and Claude, connects in under a minute, and is free for 25 checks per month. [e001:f03] AI assistants are increasingly used for research, analysis, writing, data analysis, sales, customer support and business decisions. [e001:f04] FALCON Verify makes AI trustworthy.” — Deepesh Desai, Founder and CEO But confidence is not evidence, and a confident answer is not necessarily a reliable one. [e001:f05] FALCON Verify was built to help answer that question. [e001:f06] A 2025 EBU/BBC study found 45% of more than 3,000 AI responses contained at least one significant issue. [e001:f07] Stanford researchers found 17–33% hallucination rates in specialized AI legal research tools. [e001:f08] In One Intelligence’s internal SEC filing tests, 54% of AI-generated statements were not supported by the provided filing. [e001:f09] Then Ask FALCON: FALCON Verify adds one simple step to the way people already use AI. [e001:f10] After connecting FALCON to ChatGPT or Claude, whenever an answer matters, the user says: “FALCON, verify that.” Related Posts Aspire Systems Introduces PAVE Methodology to Drive Greater Productivity from Enterprise AI Sep 25, 2026 Shield Launches Forge, an AI Operating System for IT Services Sep 25, 2026 Identity Intelligence From Senzing Now Available Through Claude Connectors Directory Sep 25, 2026 Prev Next 1 of 43,637 FALCON examines the AI-generated response statement by statement against available evidence and evaluates each checkable claim. [e001:f11] FALCON is designed to make the basis for verification visible rather than asking users to blindly trust another AI checking the first one. [e001:f12] For example, an AI might report that revenue grew 18% to $2.4 billion, operating margin was 21%, and guidance was raised. [e001:f13] If the source actually shows 12% growth, a 21% margin and reaffirmed guidance, FALCON checks the statements individually, identifying what is supported and what is contradicted, along with the evidence behind each verdict. [e001:f14] FALCON Verify can be added to ChatGPT or Claude as a connector and can also be integrated into software, AI agents and products. [e001:f15] The Free plan includes 25 checks per month with no credit card required, while enterprise customers can deploy FALCON within their own network. evidence.title: BeyondTrust launches new integrations with CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM
evidence.body: [e002:f01] “By bringing BeyondTrust’s identity and privilege intelligence into CrowdStrike Falcon, joint customers can connect privilege risk with threat activity, bringing identity threat prevention and detection together to accelerate investigation and response.” Closing the gap between identity prevention and detection The integrations connect several BeyondTrust Pathfinder Platform solutions with Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, including: BeyondTrust Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM), which surfaces policy changes, privilege elevation requests and blocked execution events within Falcon alongside other threat indicators. [e002:f02] By correlating identity relationships and privilege exposure insights across human, non-human and AI agent identities with Falcon threat telemetry, joint customers can bring additional identity and privilege context into Falcon to accelerate investigation and response. [e002:f03] Identity and privilege have become critical security signals Security teams are increasingly confronting attackers who gain access using legitimate, compromised credentials rather than traditional malware, making identity and privilege two of the most consequential risk surfaces in the enterprise. [e002:f04] Recent BeyondTrust Phantom Labs research has found that approximately 75% of modern attack paths exploit identity relationships rather than software vulnerabilities alone, underscoring the need to correlate identity intelligence with threat activity. [e002:f05] “Attackers increasingly exploit legitimate identities and privileges to move through enterprise environments, making identity context critical to understanding and responding to threats,” said David Manks, Vice President, Strategic Alliances at BeyondTrust. [e002:f06] BeyondTrust Password Safe, which brings privileged access insights into the Falcon console to enrich threat detection with privileged credential context. [e002:f07] BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access (PRA), which shares configuration changes, console authentications and session activity to extend visibility into cloud and network infrastructure. [e002:f08] The integrations build on BeyondTrust’s broader vision for privilege-centric identity security across human, non-human, workload and AI identities.
